newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats ready for elaborate handover protests.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats ready for elaborate handover protests.

text.p: A small group of Hong Kong pro-democracy activists erected huge banners on Sunday outside the building where on Monday night hundreds of world dignitaries are to witness the British colony's handover to China.

About a dozen protesters, from the Alliance in Support of the Patriotic Democratic Movement in China and the United Front Against the Provisional Legislature, put up bamboo scaffolding outside the Convention Centre on the Hong Kong harbour front and suspended black, red and yellow banners several storeys high.
One depicted the "goddess of liberty", symbol of the doomed 1989 Tiananmen Square democratic movement, crushed by Chinese troops with heavy loss of life.
Other banners, unfurled to face the entrance to the futuristic centre, read "Stop torturing Wei Jingsheng!", "Release Wang Dan!" and "Against the Provisional Legislature!"
Wei, a veteran dissident considered as the father of China's pro-democracy movement, is said to be in poor health after authorities punished him for fighting a fellow inmate.
Wang Dan was one of the student leaders jailed after the 1989 Tiananmen massacre.

More than a century and a half of British rule in Hong Kong draws to a close at midnight on Monday, a transition to be marked by a solemn ceremony headed by British heir to the throne Prince Charles and Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
"The establishment of the Provisional Legislature shows a short period of a dark age has come." said Andrew Cheng, a leader of the United Front.

Cheng, an elected member of the existing Legislative Council, will lose his seat along with fellow members of the pro-democracy lobby when China dissolves the chamber, undoing in a stroke the last-minute democratic reforms under last British Governor Chris Patten.
The protesters had vowed to sit in outside the Convention Centre until China's flag rises over Hong Kong. But it began to rain heavily in the evening and most of them headed for shelter.
"It's raining hard and I'm going home," said Leung Kwok Hung, a prominent activist.
Earlier, the group had released pigeons in a gesture of freedom which misfired.
Perhaps caged for too long, the birds failed to soar into the skies and crash-landed amid passing traffic and had to be rescued by police. One pigeon died under the wheels of a bus.
